critical_code_review_comments: Cache bypass rules are sensible and defensive: attachments/history/short(<12)/<3-tokens/CRM-token presence all skip cache — correct for a GLOBAL (multi-tenant) cache.
Cache HIT still persists BOTH user and assistant messages in assistant_messages — good for continuity + history UX.
SSE cache-HIT path re-chunks the cached reply in 60-char deltas so the UI code path stays uniform between miss and hit — nice touch.
TTL enforced defensively at query time via {expires_at: {$gt: now}} in _semantic_cache_lookup — no reliance on a Mongo TTL index (safer if index missing).

Consider adding an index on db.axon_semantic_cache (expires_at, created_at desc) to keep the candidate scan fast as the collection grows past a few thousand entries — currently CANDIDATE_LIMIT=200 is a soft ceiling.
server.py has ballooned to 12063 lines — heavy split candidate. Not blocking for this feature.
The `_ITALIAN_STOPWORDS` set contains a duplicate 'si' entry and 'lo'/'la' appear twice (once as pronoun, once as article) — harmless in a set but worth cleaning up.
seed_data_creation: None — used pre-existing demo@advisoros.it account and cache entries seeded automatically by the test itself (nonce-suffixed novel query for LLM path; PUN cache entry was already present from manual verification).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file test_v40_assistant_streaming_cache.py is idempotent — the novel-query test injects 5 UUID nonce tokens so Jaccard vs previous runs stays well below 0.75 and always exercises the LLM path. Uses requests with stream=True + line-by-line SSE parser (_parse_sse helper). Cache is GLOBAL — repeated runs will accumulate entries; that is by design (7d TTL cleans up automatically). Identical-hit response times consistently <0.5s.
